intent: Whiteboard fixes: shape-validate preferences + wire allow_for_hook_shebang
notes: Whiteboard 2026-08-29 finding 1: `read_preferences()` only validated top-level-is-dict + schema-tag, so a tagged payload with a wrong-shape section (e.g. `{"schema": "gator-preferences-v1", "python": []}`) slipped through as `present`; the resolver's `data["python"].get(...)` then crashed with `AttributeError`, violating the "never raises" contract and turning a broken preference into a hard failure instead of a loud degraded result.

Fix: new `_validate_preferences_shape(data)` in both `gator_core.py` copies. Type-checks every documented section (`python:` object, `hooks:` object, `notes:` string, `updated_at:` string) and every documented nested field (`python.windows_py_launcher`: string, `python.source`: string, `python.allow_for_hook_shebang`: bool). Reader runs it after the schema-tag check; wrong shape → `{state: "malformed", reason: "shape: <detail>"}`. Unknown sections still pass through (schema is additive-friendly). 5 new tests in `TestReadPreferences`: python-as-list, hooks-as-string, windows_py_launcher-as-int, allow_for_hook_shebang-as-string, unknown-top-level-section-tolerated.

Whiteboard 2026-08-29 finding 2: `python.allow_for_hook_shebang` was published in the schema, fixture, and operator procedure but the resolver ignored it — an operator could set `false` and Gator would still bake the launcher into the shebang.

Fix: resolver now reads `python.allow_for_hook_shebang` (default `true`). When `false`, treats the preference as opted-out and falls through to auto-detect. Adds `"opted-out: allow_for_hook_shebang=false"` outcome to the `checked` audit trail so operators can see the opt-out took effect. 2 new tests: `test_allow_for_hook_shebang_false_falls_through_to_auto` (mocked auto-detect returns different launcher; opt-out ensures auto wins), `test_allow_for_hook_shebang_true_default_uses_preference` (backward-compat pin — absent field defaults true, preference still used).

Operator procedure `configure-machine-preferences.md` gains a paragraph after the full-schema example explaining the actual live behavior of `allow_for_hook_shebang` (which the earlier version documented as a field without saying what it does).

Charter `scripts-core-library.md` `resolve_python_launcher_for_hooks` entry gains two new TRIPWIRE bullets: (1) `allow_for_hook_shebang: false` is live and points at its regression pin; (2) wrong-shape preference sections must degrade, not crash, and points at Finding 1 pin.

Test flake caught in-flight: my new `allow_for_hook_shebang` opt-out test initially used `auto-py.exe` as the mocked launcher filename — `_validate_launcher_candidate` rejected it with `basename-mismatch: 'auto-py.exe'` (basename must be exactly `py.exe`) and my machine's real `C:\Windows\py.exe` won tier 3 auto-detect, masking whether the opt-out logic actually fired. Fixed by using proper `py.exe` basenames in subdirectories (auto/py.exe vs opted-out/py.exe) so the assertion tests the resolver behavior, not the filename-validator side-effect.

These fixes ride the v2.10.0 release train — the bump commit (previously `c95f890`) was reset from dev when the whiteboard findings landed; I'll redo it fresh with an extended CHANGELOG note in the next commit.
